wines.name: Dry Riesling
wines.blurb: Crisp and high in acid, with citrus and stone-fruit notes; it cuts rich and spicy food well.

wines.name: Off-Dry Riesling
wines.blurb: A bright white with a touch of sweetness that balances heat and salt.

wines.name: Sauvignon Blanc
wines.blurb: Fresh, herbal and sharp; a good match for green herbs, citrus and goat cheese.

wines.name: Unoaked Chardonnay
wines.blurb: Medium-bodied and clean, with green apple and mineral notes; it suits lighter fish and poultry.

wines.name: Oaked Chardonnay
wines.blurb: Full and round, with buttery notes from oak; it fits rich sauces and creamy dishes.

wines.name: Pinot Grigio
wines.blurb: Light, crisp and simple, with pear and lemon notes for quick, bright dishes.

wines.name: Dry Chenin Blanc
wines.blurb: Medium-bodied, with bright acid and honeyed fruit; a flexible match for mild dishes.

wines.name: Grüner Veltliner
wines.blurb: Peppery, crisp and fresh; it works with green vegetables and light, savory dishes.

wines.name: Albariño
wines.blurb: Saline, citrusy and bright; a natural fit for seafood and shellfish.

wines.name: Vermentino
wines.blurb: Light and herbal with a saline edge; good with salads, herbs and grilled seafood.

wines.name: Verdejo
wines.blurb: Fresh, with lime and green herb notes; it suits salads and lightly cooked fish.

wines.name: Muscadet
wines.blurb: Very dry, tight and lean; it pairs with raw shellfish and light, briny dishes.

wines.name: Viognier
wines.blurb: Perfumed and full, with apricot and floral notes; it suits curries and rich, spiced dishes.

wines.name: Gewürztraminer
wines.blurb: Aromatic and textured, with lychee and rose notes; it handles spice and mild sweetness.

wines.name: Torrontés
wines.blurb: Aromatic and floral with a dry finish; a fit for fresh, herbed and citrus-forward dishes.

wines.name: Soave
wines.blurb: Light and nutty, with citrus and almond notes; it suits delicate pasta and white meats.

wines.name: Provence Rosé
wines.blurb: Pale, dry and fresh, with red-berry notes; it works across a wide range of light dishes.

wines.name: Orange Wine
wines.blurb: White grapes fermented with their skins, giving texture and savory notes; it suits hearty vegetables.

wines.name: Prosecco
wines.blurb: Light and fruity, with apple and pear notes; an easy match for fried and salty snacks.

wines.name: Cava
wines.blurb: Dry Spanish sparkling wine with citrus and bready notes; it fits tapas and fried food.

wines.name: Blanc de Blancs
wines.blurb: Made only from white grapes, with fine bubbles and toasty notes; good with creamy and salty food.

wines.name: Blanc de Noirs
wines.blurb: Sparkling wine from red grapes, with more body and red-fruit notes; it suits roast and fried dishes.

wines.name: Demi-Sec Sparkling
wines.blurb: Sparkling and sweet; a match for fruit desserts and salty-sweet dishes.

wines.name: Moscato d'Asti
wines.blurb: Lightly fizzy and sweet, with peach and orange-blossom notes; it suits fruit and light pastry.

wines.name: Sauternes
wines.blurb: Rich and sweet, with honey and apricot notes; it pairs with rich desserts and blue cheese.

wines.name: Late-Harvest Riesling
wines.blurb: Sweet and bright, with enough acid to balance the sugar; it suits fruit tarts and spiced desserts.

wines.name: Tokaji Aszú
wines.blurb: Honeyed, sweet and tangy from botrytized grapes; it suits fruit desserts and rich cheese.

wines.name: Tawny Port
wines.blurb: Fortified and sweet, with nutty and dried-fruit notes; it works with caramel desserts and hard cheese.

wines.name: Fino Sherry
wines.blurb: Dry, pale and saline, with almond notes; it suits olives, nuts and cured meats.

wines.name: Pedro Ximénez Sherry
wines.blurb: Dark, very sweet and raisiny; it pairs with dark chocolate and vanilla desserts.

wines.name: Gamay (Beaujolais)
wines.blurb: Juicy and light, with berry and floral notes; it suits chicken, salads and mild pork.

wines.name: Pinot Noir
wines.blurb: Light-bodied and silky, with red-fruit and earthy notes; it suits salmon, mushrooms and roast poultry.

wines.name: Dolcetto
wines.blurb: Soft and dry, with plum and almond notes; it suits cured meats and everyday pasta.

wines.name: Valpolicella
wines.blurb: Light and cherry-toned with bright acid; it suits tomato sauces and cured meats.

wines.name: Chianti
wines.blurb: Medium-bodied and tart, with cherry and herb notes; a classic match for tomato and grilled meat.

wines.name: Rioja
wines.blurb: Medium-bodied, with red fruit, vanilla and leather notes; it suits roast meat and grilled vegetables.

wines.name: Merlot
wines.blurb: Soft and plummy with moderate tannin; it suits roast chicken and mushroom dishes.

wines.name: Grenache Blend
wines.blurb: Warm and fruity, with spice and herb notes; it fits roasted and herbed meats.

wines.name: Barbera
wines.blurb: High-acid and plummy with low tannin; it suits tomato dishes and fatty pork.

wines.name: Zinfandel
wines.blurb: Ripe and jammy, with peppery spice notes; it suits barbecue and bold, smoky dishes.

wines.name: Cabernet Sauvignon
wines.blurb: Full and firm, with dark fruit and structured tannin; it suits grilled red meat and hard cheese.

wines.name: Bordeaux-Style Blend
wines.blurb: A structured blend with dark fruit and firm tannin; it suits roast beef and rich, savory dishes.

wines.name: Malbec
wines.blurb: Dark and plummy with soft tannin; it suits grilled beef, sausage and roasted peppers.

wines.name: Syrah
wines.blurb: Dark and peppery with smoky notes; it suits grilled and smoked meats and bold spice.

wines.name: Barolo
wines.blurb: Firm and high in tannin, with rose and tar notes; it suits braised beef and aged cheese.

wines.name: Brunello di Montalcino
wines.blurb: Full, firm Sangiovese with cherry and leather notes; it suits roast game and hearty stews.

wines.name: Carménère
wines.blurb: Plush and herbal, with dark fruit and pepper notes; it suits roast lamb and grilled vegetables.

wines.name: Aglianico
wines.blurb: Deep and firm, with high acid and tannin; it suits rich braises and aged cheese.

wines.name: Lambrusco
wines.blurb: Frothy red sparkling wine with cherry and berry notes; a bright match for tomato, cured meat and fried dough.

wines.name: Sparkling Rosé
wines.blurb: Pink, dry bubbles with red-berry and citrus notes; it suits salmon, shellfish and fried snacks.

wines.name: Nero d'Avola
wines.blurb: Ripe, dark-cherry red from Sicily with soft tannin; it suits tomato sauces and grilled sausage.

wines.name: Montepulciano d'Abruzzo
wines.blurb: Plummy and round with soft tannin; it suits pizza, pasta with meat sauce and roast chicken.

others.name: Pilsner
others.blurb: Crisp, dry and lightly bitter lager; it cuts rich, fried and salty food.

others.name: Helles Lager
others.blurb: Soft, malty pale lager with light bready notes; it fits grilled chicken and mild cheese.

others.name: Hefeweizen
others.blurb: Wheat beer with banana and clove notes; it suits citrusy salads and soft cheese.

others.name: Witbier
others.blurb: Cloudy wheat ale with orange peel and coriander; it suits fresh herbs and seafood.

others.name: Saison
others.blurb: Dry, spicy farmhouse ale with bright acidity; it suits roast chicken and fresh vegetables.

others.name: Pale Ale
others.blurb: Balanced, hoppy ale with citrus and resin notes; it fits burgers and tacos.

others.name: India Pale Ale
others.blurb: Bold, hoppy ale with piney notes; it suits spicy and fatty foods.

others.name: Amber Ale
others.blurb: Malty and toasted, with caramel notes and moderate hops; it fits roast pork and barbecue.

others.name: Brown Ale
others.blurb: Nutty and roasted, with chocolate notes; it suits nuts, roast dishes and cocoa desserts.

others.name: Porter
others.blurb: Dark, roasted and smooth, with cocoa and coffee notes; it fits smoked meat and chocolate desserts.

others.name: Stout
others.blurb: Dry, roasted and creamy; it suits oysters, rich stews and dark chocolate.

others.name: Dry Cider
others.blurb: Crisp, tart apple cider; it suits pork, sausage and sharp cheese.

others.name: Sweet Cider
others.blurb: Soft and apple-forward with a touch of sweetness; it suits spicy sausage and fruit desserts.

others.name: Blanco Tequila
others.blurb: Clear agave spirit with bright, peppery notes; it fits citrus, grilled fish and lime-forward dishes.

others.name: Aged Rum
others.blurb: Rum matured in wood, with vanilla and caramel notes; it suits sweet desserts and roast dishes.

others.name: Bourbon
others.blurb: Corn-forward whiskey with vanilla, caramel and oak notes; it suits barbecue, glazed meat and pecan desserts.

others.name: Margarita
others.blurb: A tart, lime-forward tequila drink; it cuts fried and salty food.

steps: Shake the tequila, lime juice and orange liqueur with ice.
Strain into a salt-rimmed glass.
Serve over ice or up.

others.name: Gin and Tonic
others.blurb: Dry gin with bitter tonic and lime; it suits seafood and light salads.

steps: Fill a glass with ice.
Add the gin, then the tonic water.
Squeeze in the lime wedge and stir once.

others.name: Mojito
others.blurb: Mint, lime and rum topped with soda; it suits grilled fish and spicy tacos.

steps: Gently press the mint with the lime juice in a glass.
Add the rum and ice.
Top with soda water and stir.

others.name: Old Fashioned
others.blurb: Bourbon stirred with sugar and bitters; it suits roast meat and dark desserts.

steps: Stir the sugar, bitters and a splash of water in a glass.
Add the bourbon and ice, then stir well.
Express the orange peel over the glass and drop it in.

others.name: Whiskey Highball
others.blurb: Whiskey and soda, long and light; it suits grilled meat and salty snacks.

steps: Fill a tall glass with ice.
Pour in the whiskey.
Top with soda and add the lemon twist.

others.name: Moscow Mule
others.blurb: Vodka, lime and ginger beer; it suits fried chicken and spicy Asian food.

steps: Fill a mug with ice.
Add the vodka and lime juice.
Top with ginger beer and garnish with the lime wedge.

others.name: Kölsch
others.blurb: Crisp, light ale with soft fruit notes; it suits salads, fish and light cheese.

others.name: Dunkel
others.blurb: Dark lager with toasty, bready notes; it suits roast pork and sausages.

others.name: Berliner Weisse
others.blurb: Tart, pale wheat beer with low alcohol; it suits fresh salads, soft goat cheese and fruit.

others.name: Mexican-Style Lager
others.blurb: Light, crisp lager with corn notes and citrus lift; it suits tacos, grilled meat and spicy salsa.

others.name: Bitter Aperitivo Spritz
others.blurb: Bitter-sweet, low-strength aperitivo with soda; it cuts rich, fried and cured foods.

steps: Fill a wine glass with ice.
Add the aperitivo and vermouth.
Top with soda water and garnish with the orange slice.

others.name: Reposado tequila
others.blurb: Rested 2 to 12 months in oak; soft agave with light vanilla; sips neat or on the rocks with rich, smoky or citrusy food.

others.name: Añejo tequila
others.blurb: Aged 1 to 3 years; rounder and more caramel; neat, with grilled meat or chocolate.

others.name: Mezcal
others.blurb: Smoky agave spirit; neat with a slice of orange; good with charred, fatty or spicy food.

others.name: Junmai sake
others.blurb: Pure rice sake, fuller and a little earthy; warm or chilled with savory, umami-rich food.

others.name: Ginjo or daiginjo sake
others.blurb: More polished rice, light and aromatic; serve chilled with delicate fish, rice and lighter dishes.

others.name: Nigori sake
others.blurb: Cloudy, slightly sweet and creamy; chilled with spicy food or dessert.

others.name: Vodka
others.blurb: Clean, neutral spirit; cold and in small pours, it resets the palate next to salty, smoked or pickled food.

others.name: Gin
others.blurb: Juniper and citrus botanicals; crisp with seafood, cucumber, herbs and light salads.

others.name: White rum
others.blurb: Light, grassy cane spirit; fresh with lime, mint, seafood and tropical fruit.

others.name: Spiced rum
others.blurb: Rum with vanilla, cinnamon and clove; it suits grilled pineapple, pork and sweet desserts.

others.name: Aguardiente (anise)
others.blurb: Colombian anise-flavored cane spirit, sipped cold in small shots; it goes with grilled meat, empanadas and salty snacks.

others.name: Scotch whisky
others.blurb: Malt whisky, from soft and honeyed to smoky and peaty; neat or with a drop of water next to smoked fish, lamb or aged cheese.

others.name: Irish whiskey
others.blurb: Smooth, lightly fruity triple-distilled whiskey; easy next to roast chicken, stews and apple desserts.

others.name: Rye whiskey
others.blurb: Spicier and drier than bourbon; it suits charred meat, pepper crusts and dark chocolate.

others.name: Cognac or brandy
others.blurb: Grape spirit aged in oak, with dried fruit and vanilla; after dinner, with cheese, nuts or chocolate.

others.name: Pisco
others.blurb: Unaged grape spirit from Peru and Chile, floral and clean; with ceviche, seafood and citrusy dishes.

others.name: Coffee liqueur
others.blurb: Sweet coffee liqueur; over ice or in dessert drinks, with chocolate, vanilla or caramel desserts.

others.name: Orange liqueur
others.blurb: Sweet orange-peel liqueur; a cocktail builder, and a sip with chocolate or citrus desserts.

others.name: Irish cream liqueur
others.blurb: Cream, whiskey and cocoa; over ice or in coffee, with brownies and cookies.

others.name: Amaretto
others.blurb: Sweet almond-flavored liqueur; with biscotti, fruit tarts and coffee.

others.name: Limoncello
others.blurb: Sweet lemon liqueur served ice-cold after a meal; with lemon desserts, fruit and light cakes.

cocktails.name: Vodka Soda
cocktails.mix: Vodka and soda water over ice, with a lime wedge.

steps: Fill a highball with ice and add the vodka.
Top with soda water.
Squeeze the lime wedge in and drop it.

cocktails.name: Moscow Mule
cocktails.mix: Vodka, lime juice and ginger beer, served over ice.
cocktails.food: Spicy Asian food, fried chicken, carnitas.

steps: Fill a mug or highball with ice; add vodka and lime juice.
Top with ginger beer and stir once.
Garnish with the lime wheel.

cocktails.name: Bloody Mary
cocktails.mix: Vodka, tomato juice, lemon juice, hot sauce, Worcestershire and pepper.
cocktails.food: Brunch, eggs, crispy potatoes, smoked fish.

steps: Add everything to a shaker with ice and roll it (pour back and forth), do not shake.
Strain into an ice-filled glass.
Garnish with celery and a lemon wedge.

cocktails.name: Cosmopolitan
cocktails.mix: Vodka, cranberry juice, lime juice and orange liqueur, shaken.

steps: Shake everything with ice until the shaker frosts.
Strain into a chilled coupe.
Garnish with an orange twist.

cocktails.name: Espresso Martini
cocktails.mix: Vodka, fresh espresso, coffee liqueur and simple syrup, shaken hard.

steps: Pull the espresso and let it cool a minute.
Shake everything hard with ice for 15 seconds.
Strain into a chilled coupe; the foam settles on top.

cocktails.name: Gin and Tonic
cocktails.mix: Gin and tonic water over ice, with a lime wedge.

steps: Fill the glass with ice and add the gin.
Pour the tonic down the side to keep the bubbles.
Squeeze and drop the lime.

cocktails.name: Negroni
cocktails.mix: Gin, bitter red aperitif and sweet vermouth, stirred over ice; orange peel.
cocktails.food: Cured ham, aged cheese, roasted meats.

steps: Stir the three with ice for 20 seconds.
Strain over one big ice cube.
Twist the orange peel over the top and drop it in.

cocktails.name: Tom Collins
cocktails.mix: Gin, lemon juice, simple syrup and soda water, over ice.
cocktails.food: Fried fish, crab cakes, summer salads.

steps: Shake gin, lemon and syrup with ice.
Strain into an ice-filled tall glass.
Top with soda and garnish with a lemon wheel.

cocktails.name: Gimlet
cocktails.mix: Gin and lime juice, shaken with simple syrup.

steps: Shake with ice.
Strain into a chilled coupe.
Garnish with a lime wheel.

cocktails.name: Mojito
cocktails.mix: White rum, lime juice, mint, sugar and soda water, muddled over ice.

steps: Muddle the mint gently with the sugar and lime juice in the glass.
Add rum, fill with ice and stir.
Top with soda and a mint sprig.

cocktails.name: Daiquiri
cocktails.mix: White rum, lime juice and simple syrup, shaken and strained.
cocktails.food: Grilled shrimp, coconut desserts, tropical fruit.

steps: Shake hard with ice.
Strain into a chilled coupe.
Garnish with a lime wheel.

cocktails.name: Cuba Libre
cocktails.mix: White rum, lime juice and cola over ice.

steps: Fill with ice; add rum and lime juice.
Top with cola and stir once.
Drop a lime wedge in.

cocktails.name: Margarita
cocktails.mix: Tequila, lime juice and orange liqueur, shaken; salt rim optional.
cocktails.food: Tacos, grilled fish, anything with lime and chile.

steps: Run a lime wedge around the rim and dip it in salt.
Shake tequila, lime and orange liqueur with ice.
Strain over fresh ice.

cocktails.name: Paloma
cocktails.mix: Tequila, grapefruit soda and lime juice, over ice with a salt rim.
cocktails.food: Fried snacks, shrimp tacos, spicy salsa.

steps: Salt the rim and fill the glass with ice.
Add tequila and lime juice.
Top with grapefruit soda and stir once.

cocktails.name: Ranch Water
cocktails.mix: Tequila, lime juice and sparkling mineral water over ice.

steps: Fill a tall glass with ice.
Add tequila and lime juice.
Top with sparkling water and a lime wedge.

cocktails.name: Tequila Sunrise
cocktails.mix: Tequila, orange juice and grenadine, poured so it settles in layers.

steps: Fill with ice, add tequila and orange juice, stir.
Pour the grenadine slowly down the inside; it sinks.
Garnish with an orange slice and do not stir.

cocktails.name: Mezcal Margarita
cocktails.mix: Mezcal, lime juice and orange liqueur, shaken; chile salt optional.

steps: Rim the glass with chile salt.
Shake mezcal, lime and orange liqueur with ice.
Strain over fresh ice.

cocktails.name: Mezcal Paloma
cocktails.mix: Mezcal, grapefruit soda and lime juice, over ice.

steps: Fill the glass with ice; add mezcal and lime.
Top with grapefruit soda.
Garnish with a grapefruit wedge.

cocktails.name: Old Fashioned
cocktails.mix: Bourbon or rye, sugar, bitters and orange peel, stirred over ice.

steps: Muddle the sugar with the bitters and a splash of water.
Add the whiskey and one big ice cube; stir 20 seconds.
Express the orange peel over the glass and drop it in.

cocktails.name: Whiskey Sour
cocktails.mix: Whiskey, lemon juice and simple syrup, shaken; optional egg white.
cocktails.food: Pork belly, barbecue ribs, sharp cheddar.

steps: With egg white, shake once without ice, then again with ice.
Strain over fresh ice.
Garnish with a cherry or a lemon wheel.

cocktails.name: Manhattan
cocktails.mix: Rye or bourbon, sweet vermouth and bitters, stirred and strained.

steps: Stir with ice for 20 to 30 seconds.
Strain into a chilled coupe.
Garnish with a cherry.

cocktails.name: Hot Toddy
cocktails.mix: Whiskey, honey, lemon and hot water, with a clove or cinnamon stick.
cocktails.food: Soups, sweet baked goods, roast chicken.

steps: Dissolve the honey in the hot water in a mug.
Add whiskey and lemon juice; stir.
Add the clove or cinnamon stick.

cocktails.name: Sidecar
cocktails.mix: Brandy, orange liqueur and lemon juice, shaken; sugar rim optional.

steps: Sugar the rim if you like.
Shake with ice.
Strain into a chilled coupe.

cocktails.name: Sake Spritz
cocktails.mix: Sake, soda water and a splash of citrus, over ice.

ingredients: splash of yuzu or lemon juice
steps: Fill a wine glass with ice.
Add sake and the citrus.
Top with soda and stir once.

cocktails.name: Bitter Orange Aperitif Spritz
cocktails.mix: Bitter orange aperitif, sparkling wine and soda water, over ice with an orange slice.

steps: Fill a wine glass with ice.
Pour the sparkling wine, then the aperitif, then the soda.
Add the orange slice.

cocktails.name: Mimosa
cocktails.mix: Sparkling wine and orange juice, in equal parts.

steps: Pour the sparkling wine into a flute.
Top gently with orange juice.
No ice; serve right away.

cocktails.name: Kalimotxo
cocktails.mix: Red wine and cola, in equal parts, over ice.

steps: Fill a tall glass with ice.
Pour wine and cola in equal parts.
Squeeze the lemon wedge in.

cocktails.name: White Wine Spritzer
cocktails.mix: White wine and soda water, in equal parts, over ice with a lemon twist.
cocktails.food: Light salads, grilled fish, goat cheese.

steps: Fill a wine glass with ice.
Pour the wine and top with soda.
Twist the lemon peel over it.

cocktails.name: Michelada
cocktails.mix: Lager, lime juice, hot sauce, Worcestershire and salt, over ice.
cocktails.food: Tacos, fried seafood, peanuts and fresh fruit.

steps: Salt the rim and fill the glass with ice.
Add lime juice, hot sauce and Worcestershire.
Pour the beer slowly and stir once.

zeroProof.name: Dealcoholized Sparkling Wine
zeroProof.blurb: Bubbly and dry with wine-like acidity; it suits the same foods as a dry sparkling wine.

zeroProof.name: Sparkling Water with Citrus
zeroProof.blurb: Clean bubbles and bright acid from lemon or lime; it cuts fat and salt.

zeroProof.name: Iced Black Tea
zeroProof.blurb: Brisk and gently tannic; it works with grilled and rich foods, much as a light red does.

zeroProof.name: Ginger Soda
zeroProof.blurb: Spicy and sweet with ginger heat; it suits spicy and fried foods.

zeroProof.name: Hibiscus Iced Tea
zeroProof.blurb: Tart and floral with red-berry notes; it suits grilled chicken and fruit desserts.

zeroProof.name: Dealcoholized Red Wine
zeroProof.blurb: Red-fruit and gently tannic; it suits roast vegetables and mild red meat.

principles.text: Acid in the wine cuts through fat and sweetness; a wine with less acid than the food tastes flat.
principles.label: Acid cuts fat

principles.text: Match the weight: a light dish suits a light wine, and a rich dish needs a wine with similar body.
principles.label: Match the weight

principles.text: Tannin softens when it meets protein and fat, which bind to it, so tannic reds suit rich, fatty food.
principles.label: Tannin likes protein

principles.text: Sweet food makes a dry wine taste thin and sour, so pick a wine that is at least as sweet as the dish.
principles.label: Sweet needs sweeter

principles.text: Use salt with care: a very salty dish can make tannin and sharp acid in the wine taste harsher.
principles.label: Salt softens wine

principles.text: Alcohol can cut through rich, fatty food or balance a sweet dish, so high-alcohol wines can help there.
principles.label: Alcohol cuts richness

principles.text: A contrast pairing uses acidity, tannin or sweetness in the wine to counter a dish and act as a bridge between flavors.
principles.label: Contrast as a bridge

principles.text: Regional pairs grow together: a wine from the same place as the dish often fits it, because both evolved side by side.
principles.label: Grown together

avoidReasons.text: A tannic red next to a light, lean dish tastes harsh.
A dry wine next to a sweet dish tastes thin and sour.
A low-acid wine next to rich, fatty food tastes flat.
A full-bodied wine overwhelms a light, delicate dish.
A light wine gets lost against a heavy, rich dish.
A very salty dish makes tannin and sharp acid taste harsher.
Two very acidic things together can taste sharp and clash.
A full red served too cold hides its aromas and feels harsh.
A chilled white served too warm tastes flabby.
Heavy oak flavor can hide a delicate dish.
A sweet wine next to a sour dish can taste flat and cloying.
A soft, low-acid wine disappears next to a sharp sauce.

serve.wine: Chill whites, rosé and sparkling; reds a little cooler than the room.
serve.spirit: Neat or on the rocks; a small pour.
serve.sake: Chilled or gently warm; the label says which.
serve.cocktail: Build it cold, serve right away.
serve.other: Serve the way the label suggests.
